title: Counterdiabatic quantum optimization for efficient state preparation in the Schwinger model
authors: Ethan Laval, Bipasha Chakraborty, Stefano Cipolla
abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), whose design is underpinned by the adiabatic theorem, is one of the leading variational quantum algorithms for preparing the ground states of gauge theories. A recently proposed variant, DC-QAOA, incorporates counterdiabatic driving to accelerate the adiabatic process, reducing both circuit depth and runtime. In this work, we present a systematic analysis, from both theoretical and computational perspectives, of DC-QAOA and related counterdiabatic variants for preparing the ground state of the Schwinger model, the paradigmatic (1+1)-dimensional lattice gauge theory. Benchmarking these methods against standard QAOA, we show that counterdiabatic driving improves ground-state preparation while lowering circuit depth requirements. Our results establish counterdiabatic protocols as a practical route towards efficient quantum simulation of gauge theories.
summary: This paper investigates using counterdiabatic driving to enhance quantum algorithms for finding the ground state of the Schwinger model. By comparing DC-QAOA and related CD variants against standard QAOA, the authors demonstrate that CD protocols offer a practical and resource-efficient route for simulating lattice gauge theories on quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently preparing the ground state of lattice gauge theories, specifically the Schwinger model, using quantum computation.
main_result: Counterdiabatic (CD) driving protocols, implemented in DC-QAOA, are shown to improve ground-state preparation compared to standard QAOA, achieving better performance in terms of circuit depth and resource cost.
method: The authors systematically analyze and compare several quantum algorithms, including QAOA, DC-QAOA, and CD-inspired variants, by minimizing expectation values derived from the Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Schwinger model, a paradigmatic (1+1)-dimensional lattice gauge theory, whose Hamiltonian is mapped onto Pauli gates via the Jordan-Wigner transformation.
key_observables: Best approximation ratio and best state fidelity between the final ansatz state and the true ground state of the Hamiltonian.
important_parameters: Number of qubits (up to 10), number of QAOA layers ($p$), and variational parameters ($\gamma,  eta, \alpha$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating continuous evolution using Trotterization and assumes that CD driving can accelerate the adiabatic process significantly.
figures_summary: Figures compare best approximation ratios and state fidelities for QAOA vs. CD variants across varying qubit numbers and layers, showing CD methods often outperform QAOA.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for CD-QAOA, details the specific CD-QAOA variants (CD-inspired, CD-mixer, CD-prob), and concludes with systematic computational benchmarking comparing these methods against standard QAOA.
why_interesting: The work directly compares resource-efficient quantum algorithms (CD-QAOA) against standard variational methods (QAOA) for simulating complex quantum field theories, providing benchmarks for NISQ-era quantum simulation.
